findings.description: publicly_accessible = true exposes the MySQL instance to the internet. Combined with the inbound rule allowing all of the VPC CIDR on 3306 and a hard-coded 'admin' username, any host that can route to the endpoint can attempt to authenticate directly against the database.
storage_encrypted = false leaves the database volume, snapshots, and replicas unencrypted, so anyone with access to the underlying storage or a snapshot can read the data in plaintext.

The user_data script embeds the database endpoint, username, and the literal database password (var.password) into a PHP file written to disk, and user_data is readable via the EC2 instance metadata service by any process or SSRF vulnerability on the host, permanently exposing the DB credential.

The policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", giving the instance role full control of storage, compute, and databases account-wide. A compromise of this EC2 instance yields complete control over data and infrastructure well beyond what the application needs.
The ingress rule opens MySQL port 3306 to the entire VPC CIDR block rather than restricting it to the application server's security group, letting any workload in the VPC reach the database directly.
The egress rule permits all protocols to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing the database security group's members to exfiltrate data or reach arbitrary external hosts if compromised.

The master username is the well-known default 'admin', which removes the effort required to guess a valid high-privilege account name and materially increases the likelihood of a successful credential-guessing attack against the publicly reachable instance.

The trust policy allows sts:AssumeRole to ec2.amazonaws.com without any condition (aws:SourceArn, aws:SourceAccount, or instance-profile scoping) and with an empty Sid, so the role can be assumed by any EC2 instance that can satisfy the trust relationship.
